package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate IP utility libraries but contain obfuscated code that downloads and executes OS-specific trojan and info-stealer binaries from a remote server. The packages are part of a broader typosquatting campaign targeting developers with malware.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code determines the OS, downloads an OS-specific binary from 95.216.251.178, writes it to disk, and executes it, resulting in remote code execution and potential info-stealing or trojan activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate IP utility libraries should not download or execute remote binaries. The use of obfuscated code and hardcoded external IPs is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal IP checker would only perform local IP address parsing or make a simple HTTP request to a public IP service, not download and execute binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated updaters or installers may download binaries, but never in a utility library context and never without user consent.
key_indicators: OS detection logic to select payload

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package, triggering execution of obfuscated code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of OS-specific malicious binary.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads a trojan/info-stealer binary from 95.216.251.178 based on the user's OS.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the downloaded binary on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Downloaded binary (e.g., svchost.exe, gsd-mouse, node) is executed, performing info-stealing, trojan, or cryptocurrency stealing activities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of the victim's system and exfiltration of sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or install-time download and execution of remote binaries
OS detection logic followed by network requests to hardcoded IPs
Execution of non-standard binaries from temporary directories
file_indicators: Downloaded binaries named svchost.exe, gsd-mouse, node in /tmp or %TEMP%
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to non-standard IPs during package import or install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages containing obfuscated code that performs OS detection and downloads executables from hardcoded IP addresses. Flag any package that writes and executes binaries during import or install. Watch for network connections to 95.216.251.178 or similar suspicious endpoints, especially if triggered by utility libraries. Alert on unexpected process creation from Node.js processes in the context of package usage.
